## What this guide covers

SurveyDokum's workflow has two parts:

1. **One-off package-scaffolding steps** — creating a new R package for your dataset,
   the folder structure, and building a documentation website. These use general-purpose
   **usethis** and **pkgdown** tools directly -- SurveyDokum does not wrap them in its
   own functions, because they are not steps specific to survey data (see "Why these
   steps are not their own functions" at the end).
2. **Working with and documenting the survey data itself** — this is where SurveyDokum
   provides its `sd_`-prefixed functions: reading the data, detecting variable roles,
   statistics, LLM-based descriptive documentation, roxygen2 documentation, and a
   codebook.

This guide walks through both parts as a single path from start to finish. The details
and parameters of individual `sd_` functions are in their own help pages (e.g.
`?sd_read`, `?sd_summarise`, `?sd_document`).

This vignette is a parallel English-language translation of the package's Finnish
vignette ("Uuden surveypaketin perustaminen SurveyDokumin avulla") -- there is also a
Swedish version ("Komma igång med SurveyDokum"). All three cover the same workflow.

## Prerequisites

Install the required packages beforehand:

```r
install.packages(c("usethis", "devtools", "roxygen2", "pkgdown"))
install.packages(c("ellmer", "haven", "readxl", "codebook", "rmarkdown"))
```

The LLM-based steps (`sd_document()`, `sd_generate_roxygen()`) additionally require a
locally installed and running copy of [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) with a model
already pulled, e.g.:

```sh
ollama pull gemma3:12b
```

You can check the Ollama connection beforehand with `sd_check_ollama()`.

## Step 1: Create a package skeleton for the new dataset

Each documented survey dataset gets its own small R package -- the same way SurveyDokum
itself is built. `usethis::create_package()` opens a new RStudio window; continue the
remaining steps in that window.

```r
usethis::create_package("path/MySurvey")
```

## Step 2: Create the folder structure

```r
usethis::use_data_raw("data")   # creates data-raw/data.R

dir.create("inst/methodology", recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("inst/codebook",    recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("inst/extdata",     recursive = TRUE)
```

Remember to add `SurveyDokum` to the new package's `DESCRIPTION` file, under `Imports`
or `Suggests` (e.g. `usethis::use_dev_package("SurveyDokum")` if SurveyDokum has not
been published on CRAN).

## Step 3: Read and prepare the data

```r
library(SurveyDokum)

data <- sd_read("data-raw/mysurvey.sav")   # csv/tsv/xlsx/xls/sav/dta/rds

# Missing-value codes are cleaned up before role detection:
data <- sd_set_missing(data, codes = c(-9, -1))

# Automatic variable role detection (id/nominal/likert/continuous/date/text):
data <- sd_detect_roles(data)

# Check the result and correct by hand if needed:
data$meta$roles
data <- sd_set_role(data, "some_variable", "nominal")

# Statistical summary -- open-text variables show only aggregates, never
# individual responses:
summary_stats <- sd_summarise(data)
print(summary_stats)
```

## Step 4: Save the data into the package

```r
survey_data <- sd_get_data(data)
usethis::use_data(survey_data, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Step 5: Documentation -- a human-readable description and roxygen2

Human-readable, LLM-written description (e.g. for methodology documentation):

```r
documentation <- sd_document(data, model = "gemma3:12b", language = "en")
print(documentation)   # read the result carefully before saving

# Once the text looks good:
sd_document(data, model = "gemma3:12b", language = "en", save_to = "inst/methodology/description.txt")
```

`roxygen2` data documentation for the `?survey_data` help page:

```r
roxygen_result <- sd_generate_roxygen(data, "survey_data", language = "en")   # dry_run = TRUE by default
print(roxygen_result)   # check the text before writing it to disk

# Once the text looks good, write it to R/survey_data.R:
sd_generate_roxygen(data, "survey_data", language = "en", dry_run = FALSE)

devtools::document()
?survey_data   # check the result
```

Both `sd_document()` and `sd_generate_roxygen()` accept a `language` parameter
(default `"fi"`; also supports `"en"` and `"sv"`) that controls the language the LLM
writes its generated descriptive text in -- independently of the language the
dataset's own variable labels happen to be in. This is how the same dataset can be
documented in Finnish, English, or Swedish depending on your audience, as shown above
with `language = "en"`.

Note: this does not affect how the statistics themselves
(`sd_summarise()`/`format()`) are displayed, which is currently always in Finnish --
only the instructions given to the LLM and the text it writes change.

## Step 5b: Updating the documentation when the dataset gains new variables

As a research project progresses, a dataset often grows new variables -- sum scores
computed from earlier questions, or a new wave of questions added. Re-running
`sd_generate_roxygen()` would rewrite the whole `\describe{}` block from scratch,
discarding any description text you had already reviewed and approved. Instead, use:

```r
# Quickly check (no LLM call) whether the documentation is up to date:
sd_check_documentation_current(data, "survey_data")
```

If new, undocumented variables are found, `sd_update_roxygen()` asks the LLM for
descriptions of ONLY those variables -- the title, `@details`, `@source`, and
previously documented variables are left untouched, and the `@format` line's variable
count is updated automatically:

```r
# the dataset now contains, say, a new sum variable "tt_mean":
update <- sd_update_roxygen(data, "survey_data", language = "en")   # dry_run = TRUE by default
print(update)   # check the added descriptions before saving

# Once the text looks good:
sd_update_roxygen(data, "survey_data", language = "en", dry_run = FALSE)
devtools::document()
```

`dry_run = FALSE` always takes a backup of the previous file
(`R/survey_data.R.bak`) before writing, so an unwanted update can be undone by
restoring that backup. New variables are detected automatically by comparing the
dataset's variables against what is already documented -- if you want to describe the
variables in an order you choose yourself, or automatic detection does not work
(e.g. a heavily hand-edited file), pass them with the `new_vars` parameter instead:

```r
sd_update_roxygen(data, "survey_data", new_vars = c("tt_mean", "tt_category"), language = "en")
```

`sd_update_roxygen()` also accepts the `language` parameter, the same way as
`sd_generate_roxygen()` (see above) -- it should normally match the language the
existing text in the file is already written in.

This pair of functions (`sd_check_documentation_current()`/`sd_update_roxygen()`)
covers only NEW VARIABLES. For the situation where the variables stay the same
but the dataset gains new rows (respondents), see the next section, Step 5c.

## Step 5c: When the dataset gains new rows (respondents)

The opposite situation can also arise: the variables stay the same, but new
rows are added to the dataset (e.g. a new wave of the same survey). In that
case the `\describe{}` block needs no change at all -- only the row count
recorded in the roxygen2 file's `@format` line (e.g. "... with 200 rows and
17 variables:") is now out of date. `sd_check_row_count()` and
`sd_update_row_count()` handle this with no LLM call at all -- unlike a
variable's description, a row count has exactly one correct value, so
there is nothing to ask a model for:

```r
# Quickly check (no LLM call) whether the documented row count matches the data:
sd_check_row_count(data, "survey_data")

# If it doesn't match, fix the @format line:
update <- sd_update_row_count(data, "survey_data")   # dry_run = TRUE by default
print(update)   # check the change before saving

# Once it looks good:
sd_update_row_count(data, "survey_data", dry_run = FALSE)
devtools::document()
```

Like `sd_update_roxygen()`, `sd_update_row_count()` always takes a `.bak`
backup before writing when `dry_run = FALSE`.

Note that `sd_update_row_count()` updates ONLY the roxygen2 file's
`@format` line -- it does not touch `sd_document()`'s descriptive text.
Because that text (e.g. the number of respondents, distributions) is
written by the LLM from the whole dataset and cannot be patched
incrementally the way new variable descriptions can, updating it is
intentionally left as a manual step -- re-run `sd_document()` if the
change in row count is significant enough to warrant it.

## Step 6: Codebook

```r
codebook <- sd_codebook(data)
codebook$file   # path to the finished HTML codebook (inst/codebook/codebook.html)
```

`sd_codebook()` automatically detects sum-score groups built from Likert-scale items
based on a shared name prefix (e.g. `tt1`, `tt2`, `tt3` → group `"tt"`). You can
override the automatic detection with the `groups` parameter if your own naming
convention is different.

## Step 7: pkgdown documentation website (optional but recommended)

```r
usethis::use_pkgdown()
usethis::use_readme_rmd()      # edit README.Rmd as you like
devtools::build_readme()
```

Edit the `_pkgdown.yml` file created at the package root as needed, e.g.:

```yaml
template:
  bootstrap: 5
  bootswatch: flatly

navbar:
  title: "My Survey"

home:
  title: "MySurvey"
  description: "Survey dataset documentation and data description"
```

Build and preview the site:

```r
pkgdown::build_site()
pkgdown::preview_site()

# You can also build only parts of it:
pkgdown::build_reference()   # only the ?-help pages
pkgdown::build_home()        # only the home page (README)
```

## Step 8: Publishing (optional)

**GitHub Pages:**

```r
usethis::use_git()
usethis::use_github()
usethis::use_pkgdown_github_pages()
```

From then on, update the site with `pkgdown::build_site()`, `git add docs/`,
`git commit`, `git push`.

**Without GitHub (a network drive / SharePoint):** the `docs/` folder is a plain
static HTML site -- copy it as-is to the location of your choice, or zip it for
distribution with `zip("documentation.zip", "docs")`.

## Why these steps are not SurveyDokum's own functions

Creating the package (`usethis::create_package()`) and building the documentation
website (`pkgdown::build_site()`) are not steps specific to survey data -- they are
general-purpose R package development tasks that usethis and pkgdown already handle
well. SurveyDokum's own value is specifically in the survey-specific steps: variable
role detection, computing statistics, LLM-based documentation, and codebook
generation -- the `sd_` functions exist for these. This keeps SurveyDokum's core small
and focused, rather than duplicating existing, well-functioning tools.

## Summary -- all commands in sequence

```r
library(usethis)
library(devtools)
library(SurveyDokum)

# 1. Package skeleton
usethis::create_package("path/MySurvey")

# --- continue in the new window ---

# 2. Folder structure
usethis::use_data_raw("data")
dir.create("inst/methodology", recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("inst/codebook",    recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("inst/extdata",     recursive = TRUE)

# 3. Reading and preparing the data
data <- sd_read("data-raw/mysurvey.sav")
data <- sd_set_missing(data, codes = c(-9, -1))
data <- sd_detect_roles(data)
summary_stats <- sd_summarise(data)

# 4. Saving into the package
survey_data <- sd_get_data(data)
usethis::use_data(survey_data, overwrite = TRUE)

# 5. Documentation
sd_document(data, language = "en", save_to = "inst/methodology/description.txt")
sd_generate_roxygen(data, "survey_data", language = "en", dry_run = FALSE)
devtools::document()

# 6. Codebook
sd_codebook(data)

# 7. pkgdown website
usethis::use_pkgdown()
usethis::use_readme_rmd()
devtools::build_readme()
pkgdown::build_site()
```
